source_caption:
To maintain the playful, childish aesthetic of a world entirely constructed out of literal toys, director Chris McKay made a highly unusual demand of his voice cast during the recording sessions for The Lego Batman Movie. Instead of relying entirely on the Skywalker Sound team to generate heavy, realistic weapon sound effects for the film’s chaotic action sequences, McKay instructed the actors to physically voice their own sound effects. Whenever a character fired a weapon on screen, the actors simply said “pew, pew, pew” into the microphone. These genuine, mouth-made noises were then layered directly over the final digital sound mix, adding an authentic layer of childlike imagination to the massive, blockbuster action scenes.

The Lego Batman Movie (2017), directed by Chris McKay, starring Will Arnett, Zach Galifianakis, Michael Cera, Rosario Dawson. A cooler-than-ever Bruce Wayne must deal with the usual suspects planning to rule Gotham City, while simultaneously discovering that he has accidentally adopted a teenage orphan who wishes to become his eager sidekick.

source_details.title: The Lego Batman Movie
source_details.synopsis: The Lego Batman Movie is a 2017 animated superhero comedy film based on characters created by DC Comics and the Lego Batman toy line. It was directed by Chris McKay from a screenplay that is based on a Seth Grahame-Smith story. The film is a collaboration between production houses from the United States, Australia and Denmark, the first spin-off in The Lego Movie franchise and the second installment overall. The film features Will Arnett reprising his role as Batman from The Lego Movie alongside Zach Galifianakis, Michael Cera, Rosario Dawson and Ralph Fiennes. The story follows Batman as he attempts to overcome his greatest fear while saving Gotham City from the Joker's latest scheme. Devel
